name: Sandisk
key_signal: After a 250%+ six-month run to a 52-week high of $2,354, SNDK has broken down technically -26.8% in the last month, now trading below its 50-day SMA with a negative MACD histogram and RSI under 42.
thesis: SanDisk is riding an historic NAND flash upcycle where AI-driven memory scarcity has pushed pricing and margins to extraordinary levels (70% operating margin, 56% gross margin, 39% ROE), and the forward P/E of 6.7x versus a trailing 49x implies the Street expects earnings to inflect dramatically higher as pricing gains flow through. The stock remains above its 200-day SMA with an intact golden cross, so the primary uptrend from the spinoff lows is technically undamaged, and a 'buy' consensus from 22 analysts suggests the Street still sees upside once the current air pocket clears.
bear_case: The magnitude of the pullback (-26.8% in 21 days, now ~39% off the 52-week high) after a parabolic 250% six-month move is a classic sign that a momentum-driven, commodity-cycle stock has entered a distribution phase — NAND pricing cycles are notoriously volatile and prone to sharp reversals once hyperscaler buying pauses or supply catches up, and the 146% annualized volatility means this could easily be the start of a much deeper drawdown rather than a pause. With price-to-book at 15.4x and debt/equity at 1.5x against a cyclical, capital-intensive commodity memory business, any disappointment on NAND ASPs or a sequential margin deceleration would crush the 6.7x forward multiple's implied earnings assumption, and the stock trading below its 50-day average with negative MACD momentum signals that near-term sentiment has already begun to price that risk in.
